# serial-broker

> A TypeScript library that shares one Web Serial port between all tabs of a web origin. One tab
> holds the port; every tab reads and writes through it; another tab takes over when the holding
> tab closes or crashes; the connection comes back when the device does. Chromium-based desktop
> browsers only (Chrome, Edge). No framing, no protocol: bytes in, bytes out.

This file tells a language model what it needs to integrate serial-broker into an application
correctly. It is complete for the common cases; the full documentation is in `docs/site/`.

## When to use it

- A web application talks to a serial device (scale, scanner, label printer, PLC, instrument,
  microcontroller) through the Web Serial API and may be open in more than one tab or window.
  Plain Web Serial gives the second tab `InvalidStateError`; serial-broker makes every tab work.
- Also useful in a single tab: automatic reconnection, a remembered device, stable error codes.

Not for: Firefox, Safari, Chrome for Android (no Web Serial, or not a target); Node.js; sharing a
port between different origins; message framing or request/response protocols (write those on top).

## Requirements

- Chromium-based desktop browser. A secure context: HTTPS, `localhost`, or a page opened from a
  file (`file://`).
- All tabs on the same origin. Note: every page opened from a file is ONE origin for the browser.
- The worker script `serial-broker.worker.js` must be served as a file of its own, at the SAME URL
  for every tab.

## Install

Not on the npm registry before 1.0. Each GitHub release attaches `serial-broker-<version>.tgz`
(`npm install ./serial-broker-<version>.tgz`) and `serial-broker-<version>-browser.zip` (the
browser files, for a page without a package manager). Where documentation says
`npm install serial-broker`, that is the command from 1.0 on.

Entry points of the package:

| Import                          | File in `dist/`                        | Use                                   |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `serial-broker`                 | `serial-broker.js` / `.cjs` + types    | bundler or native ES module           |
| `serial-broker/min`             | `serial-broker.min.js`                 | ES module without a bundler           |
| `serial-broker/global`          | `serial-broker.global.js`              | classic `<script>`, global `SerialBroker` |
| `serial-broker/worker`          | `serial-broker.worker.js`              | the worker script; serve it as a file |
| `serial-broker/diagnostics`     | `serial-broker.diagnostics.js`         | read-only view for operator tools     |

## Minimal integration (bundler, TypeScript)

```ts
import { SerialBroker, SerialBrokerStatus, isSerialBrokerError } from 'serial-broker';
import workerUrl from 'serial-broker/worker?url'; // Vite. Otherwise copy the file and pass its path.

// 1. Once, before the first setup(): where the worker script is served.
SerialBroker.configure({ workerUrl });

// 2. Register a named configuration. The name is what tabs share: same name = same device.
await SerialBroker.setup('Scale', {
  serial: { baudRate: 9600 },
  encoding: { decodeText: true }, // also deliver event.text
});

// 3. Listen. subscribe() returns a function that unsubscribes.
let buffer = ''; // one event is not one message: keep the rest until its line end arrives
SerialBroker.subscribe('Scale', 'onReceive', (event) => {
  const lines = (buffer + (event.text ?? '')).split('\n');
  buffer = lines.pop() ?? '';
  lines.forEach(handleLine);
});
SerialBroker.subscribe('Scale', 'onStatusChange', (event) => render(event.status));
SerialBroker.subscribe('Scale', 'onError', (event) => show(event.error.code, event.error.remediation));

// 4. The browser shows its port picker only during a user gesture.
connectButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
  SerialBroker.requestAccess('Scale').catch(showError); // resolves false if the picker is dismissed
});

// 5. Send: string (encoded as UTF-8 by default) or bytes. Nothing is appended.
await SerialBroker.send('Scale', new Uint8Array([0x02, 0xff, 0x03]));
await SerialBroker.send('Scale', 'T\r\n').catch(showError);
```

`setup()`, `requestAccess()` and `send()` reject with a `SerialBrokerError`: show every one of them
ON THE PAGE like `onError` (`showError` above), not only in the console - `setup()` rejects in a
browser without Web Serial. On `failed`, offer a button that calls `setup()` again.

Show the connect button exactly while the status is `awaiting-permission`. On a later visit the
port opens without a prompt: the browser remembers the permission, the library the configuration.

## Without a bundler, or opened from a file

A page opened from a file (`file://`) may load neither ES modules nor import maps, and the browser
starts no SharedWorker for it. Use the classic build with relative paths; the library then
coordinates tabs over a BroadcastChannel by itself.

```html
<script src="./serial-broker/serial-broker.global.js"></script>
<script>
  SerialBroker.configure({
    workerUrl: new URL('./serial-broker/serial-broker.worker.js', document.baseURI).href,
  });
  // SerialBroker.setup(...), .subscribe(...), .send(...) as above.
  // Also on the global: isSupported, isSerialBrokerError, hasCode, SerialBrokerStatus,
  // SerialBrokerErrorCode, SerialBrokerError, REMEDIATION, PROTOCOL_VERSION.
</script>
```

With the classic and CommonJS builds `configure({ workerUrl })` is REQUIRED before `setup()`.

## API (`SerialBroker`)

```ts
configure(options: { workerUrl?: string | URL; transport?: 'auto' | 'sharedworker' | 'broadcastchannel';
                     logger?: { log(level, message, fields): void }; logPayloads?: boolean }): void
isSupported(): boolean                       // Web Serial + Web Locks + a message bus are there
setup(name: string, options: SerialBrokerOptions): Promise<void>
requestAccess(name: string, options?: { chooseAgain?: boolean }): Promise<boolean>  // from a click
send(name: string, data: string | BufferSource): Promise<void>
subscribe(name, event, listener): () => void // events: onReceive | onSend | onError | onStatusChange
unsubscribe(name, event, listener): void
getStatus(name: string): SerialBrokerStatusSnapshot   // status, deviceKind, vendorId, productId,
                                                      // serialOptions, maxTabs, since, lastErrorCode
exists(name: string): boolean                // for THIS tab
names(): readonly string[]
restore(): Promise<readonly string[]>        // sets up every remembered configuration
release(name: string, options?: { forget?: boolean; forgetDevice?: boolean }): Promise<void>
releaseAll(options?): Promise<void>
dispose(): Promise<void>
```

### `SerialBrokerOptions` (defaults in brackets)

- `device`: which port. Omit it, or `{ auto: true }` = **auto mode**: the device is taken from the
  port the user picks, remembered, and adopted by the other tabs; `requestAccess(name, {
  chooseAgain: true })` picks another later. `{ vendorId, productId }` = a known USB device (picker
  filtered, a granted port opens without a prompt). `{ nonUsb: true }` = a port without USB
  identity. `{ any: true }` = the first granted port.
- `serial`: `baudRate` (required, 1-20,000,000), `dataBits` 7|8 [8], `stopBits` 1|2 [1], `parity`
  'none'|'even'|'odd' ['none'], `flowControl` 'none'|'hardware' ['none'], `bufferSize` [255].
- `connection`: `autoReconnect` [true], `initialDelayMs` [250], `factor` [2], `maxDelayMs` [30000],
  `jitter` [0.5], `maxAttempts` [Infinity], `stableAfterMs` [5000], `openTimeoutMs` [10000],
  `writeTimeoutMs` [5000], `maxWriteChunkBytes` [4096].
- `receive`: `idleMs` [50], `maxWaitMs` [500] - received bytes are collected until the line is
  quiet, then delivered as one `onReceive`. Use `idleMs: 0` to get every read as it arrives.
- `encoding`: `decodeText` [false] (adds `event.text`), `encoding` ['utf-8'].
- `remember` [true]: keep the configuration for `restore()` and later visits.
- `maxTabs` [Infinity]: at most N tabs use it at once; `1` = exclusive. The others are `queued`.

### Statuses

`idle` → `queued`? → `awaiting-permission`? → `connecting` → `open` ⇄ `reconnecting`; `failed`
(gave up; `setup()` again with the same options restarts it); `released` (last event of a tab).
Compare with `SerialBrokerStatus.Open` etc. A new `onStatusChange` listener is told the current
status once, immediately.

### Events

- `onReceive`: `{ name, data: Uint8Array, text: string | undefined, timestamp }` - the same in every tab.
- `onSend`: `{ name, data, origin: 'local' | 'remote', timestamp }` - every tab's writes, this one's included.
- `onStatusChange`: `{ name, status, previousStatus, timestamp }`.
- `onError`: `{ name, error: SerialBrokerError, timestamp }`.

### Errors

Every failure is a `SerialBrokerError` with a stable `code`, a `message`, a `remediation` sentence,
`isRetryable` (true = the library is recovering by itself; show it as a note), `context`,
`configName`, `timestamp`. **Branch on `code`, never on `message`.** Use `isSerialBrokerError(e)`
and `hasCode(e, 'WRITE_TIMEOUT')`.

Codes: `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `UNKNOWN_CONFIGURATION`, `CONFIGURATION_CONFLICT`,
`CONFIGURATION_RELEASED`, `WEB_SERIAL_UNAVAILABLE`, `WEB_LOCKS_UNAVAILABLE`,
`TRANSPORT_UNAVAILABLE`, `BROKER_UNAVAILABLE`, `PERMISSION_REQUIRED`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`,
`USER_GESTURE_REQUIRED`, `DEVICE_MISMATCH`, `OPEN_FAILED`, `OPEN_TIMEOUT`, `DEVICE_DISCONNECTED`,
`RECONNECT_EXHAUSTED`, `READ_FAILED`, `NOT_CONNECTED`, `WRITE_FAILED`, `WRITE_TIMEOUT`,
`WRITE_QUEUE_FULL`, `OWNER_LOST_DURING_WRITE`, `PROTOCOL_VERSION_MISMATCH`, `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`,
`STORAGE_CORRUPT`, `LISTENER_THREW`, `INTERNAL_INVARIANT`, `UNKNOWN`.

## Rules that matter

1. `configure()` before the first `setup()`. Every tab must name the same `workerUrl`.
2. Call `requestAccess()` from a click or key handler, before anything slow. The browser counts a
   click as a gesture for a few seconds; `setup()` then `requestAccess()` in one click is fine.
3. One configuration name per device, the same name in every tab. Calling `setup()` again in the
   same tab with a different device, line settings or `maxTabs` raises `CONFIGURATION_CONFLICT`:
   `release()` first. Between tabs, the tab holding the port opens it with its own line settings;
   a different `maxTabs` makes the other tab withdraw with that error.
4. **A write reaches the device at most once.** `send()` rejecting with `context.started === false`
   means nothing was written and it is safe to send again. `OWNER_LOST_DURING_WRITE` or a
   `WRITE_TIMEOUT` with `started: true` means the device MAY have received it - never retry such a
   write blindly for a command with side effects.
5. The library does no framing. One `onReceive` is "what arrived until the line went quiet", not a
   message. Split lines or frames yourself and keep a buffer across events.
6. Writes of one tab keep their order. Writes of different tabs have no defined order - if two tabs
   command one device, give one of them the job (`maxTabs: 1`, or an application rule).
7. Never ask which tab holds the port. The API does not say, on purpose: the answer is wrong a
   moment later.
8. `release(name)` forgets nothing. `{ forget: true }` drops the remembered configuration,
   `{ forgetDevice: true }` gives the browser's permission back (for every tab of the origin).
9. Data sent by the device during a handover between tabs, or while reconnecting, is lost. Design
   the device protocol so that a missed message can be asked for again.
10. Show `error.code` and `error.remediation` to the operator; log with `configure({ logger })`.
    Payload bytes are logged only with `logPayloads: true` - serial data can be sensitive.

## Typical patterns

- **Operator station, several windows:** every window `setup()`s the same name and subscribes;
  one window sends. Nothing else to do.
- **Exclusive control:** `maxTabs: 1`; show `queued` as "in use in another window".
- **Known device:** `device: { vendorId, productId }`; after the first grant it opens by itself.
- **Device chosen by the user, changeable later:** omit `device`; `requestAccess(name)` for the
  first choice, `requestAccess(name, { chooseAgain: true })` to change it.
- **No automatic reconnect:** `connection: { autoReconnect: false }`; a loss ends in `failed` until
  `setup()` is called again.
- **Request/answer:** send, then resolve on the next complete line from `onReceive`, with your own
  timeout. Every tab receives every answer, so one request at a time across ALL tabs: hold a Web
  Lock of your own (`navigator.locks.request('my-app/scale', ...)`) around send-and-wait.

## Where things are

In the repository (https://github.com/tkrepo1234/serial-broker); the package itself holds `dist/`,
`README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and this file.

- `README.md` - overview. `docs/site/` - the documentation (Sphinx, Markdown): `installing.md`,
  `first-connection.md`, `configuration.md`, `errors.md`, `shared-ports.md`, `guarantees.md`,
  `known-limits.md`, `deploying.md`, `diagnostics.md`, `examples/`.
- `examples/minimal-js/` - one HTML page, no build step. `examples/terminal-openui5/` - a serial
  terminal in SAP OpenUI5 whose build runs from a folder opened as a file.
- `dist/debug/` - a debugging surface shipped with the package (static files; serve them yourself).
- `docs/adr/` - why the library is built the way it is.
